messages:
mari: quick check — observed a ~4% p95 latency bump on private compared to hosted for the embedder model after ~72h of uptime. same model/version pinned. suspect GPU memory fragmentation or allocator drift. can infra run a short repro and collect allocator stats?

adrian: yep saw that trend in the nightly summary. curious if it's allocator (jemalloc) vs CUDA driver pages. do we have a synthetic that repeats long-running allocations?

mari: I can drop a tiny loop that allocates progressively longer sequences + KV cache churn. goal is a 10m run. will post script.

chloe: tagging @devops-jen — can you schedule a quick private-node run on dc1-private-02? low risk, non-prod. also want nvidia-smi snapshots and /proc/meminfo during the run.

devops-jen: got it, I can spin it up in the next maintenance window (in ~30m). any special env vars? MALLOC_CONF or LD_PRELOAD?

mari: please set MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true,lg_dirty_mult:16 (jemalloc) and enable CUDA_MEMCHECK=0 (we're not checking for correctness). also capture nvml allocator stats every 30s. here's the microbench:

```# microbench.py (run with python3)
import time, torch
model = torch.load('embedder.pt').cuda()
for i in range(600):
    seq = torch.randint(0,10000,(1,64 + (i%128))).cuda()
    _ = model(seq)
    if i % 30 == 0:
        print(f"iter={i}")
    time.sleep(0.5)
```

chloe: thanks — I'll attach a crontab to pull `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv` and `cat /proc/<pid>/smaps` snapshots.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: canary job finished on dc1-private-02 (no failures) :white_check_mark:

sam: quick note — if fragmentation looks like the culprit we should also try restarting the app process (not the node) to see if the allocator cleans up. that's cheaper than a full node reboot.

mari: Agreed. Plan: 1) run microbench 10m with jemalloc stats + nvml sampling 2) if regression observed, restart runtime process and rerun 3) collect jemalloc stats_print and smaps and upload to perf-buckets.

adrian: can you also capture `pmap -x <pid>` and `python -m tracemalloc` at start/end? tracemalloc might be noisy but useful for host-side leaks.

chloe: running now. will update with the raw artifacts link when done.

nora: fyi, I hit a similar drift last quarter on a long-running replica — turned out to be intermittent pinned CUDA tensors from an older bug in a data loader. might be worth grepping for `.cuda()` without `.detach()` in recent commits.

mari: good call — I'll add a quick static grep and run flake-checker rule. thanks.

chloe: run finished. initial numbers: hosted p95=48ms, private pre-restart p95=51ms, post-restart p95=48. attaching jemalloc dump and nvml csv to perf-buckets: s3://perf-buckets/2003124567/

mari: that's pretty indicative. can someone run the same job on a node that hasn't been up for 72h (fresh boot) to confirm?

devops-jen: queued a fresh node test on dc1-private-04, ETA 20m.

adrian: if fresh node matches hosted and restart fixes private, we should add a periodic restart policy to the runtime service (weekly) and track improvement. file an RFC?

mari: will write a 1-pager and propose weekly restart + jemalloc tuning. thanks all for quick help. :tada:
